items.title: The Most Capable Humanoid Robot Yet!
items.summary:
Google just released Gemini Robotics 2 today, and it's a much bigger leap than you may think.

Unlike previous models, it coordinates everything from feet to fingertips, allowing the robot to balance and walk while handling delicate objects.

With 22 degrees of movement in its hands, it can seal Ziploc bags, unscrew lightbulbs, and even tie trash bag knots.

Plus, an on-device version runs locally without an internet connection and can adapt to new robot bodies in just a few hours.

To be clear: this new release "Google Robotics 2" is the AI software behind the robot, not a physical robot you buy directly from Google. It powers hardware from partners like Apptronik on their Apollo 2 robot. 

For Developers: You can access the reasoning model "Gemini Robotics ER 2" today on Google AI Studio.
For Hardware Integrators: The full Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and On-Device models are currently available to partners through Google DeepMind's early access program.

items.title: Delhi Police's AI Van Watches Protesters, No Law Stops It | Front Page
items.summary:
A facial recognition van deployed at the CJP protest site has reignited a fight over what counts as standard policing versus mass biometric harvesting. India still has no dedicated law governing facial recognition technology, and the retention rules for the data it collects run to 75 years. 

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Merin Susan John and Novinston Lobo, Tech Journalists at AIM, to break down how India's Automated Facial Recognition System pulls from passport, prison and child-welfare databases with almost no legislative oversight, why a facial recognition regulation bill has sat dormant in Parliament since 2023, how the Criminal Procedure Act of 2022 allows biometric data to be held for 75 years, the parallel case of the UK's Met Police facial recognition ruling, and why transparency, not the technology itself, is the real fault line in this debate.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Pocket FM's Head of AI on Its $400M Storytelling Bet
